name: OmniReflect: Discovering Transferable Constitutions for LLM agents via Neuro-Symbolic Reflections
authors: Manasa Bharadwaj, Nikhil Verma, Kevin Ferreira (LG Electronics, Toronto AI Lab)
venue: arXiv preprint (also submitted to ACL ARR 2025 May, OpenReview 3xEmiKN3WH)
reflection_type: verbal-self-critique (LLM-generated natural-language reflections) combined with symbolic regular-expression progress checks; hybrid neuro-symbolic. In Co-operative mode a separate Meta-advisor agent supplies the reflections/constitution to a consumer agent
feedback_source: self-generated (LLM reflections over its own trajectory) plus external-tool symbolic signal (regular expressions extended from AgentBoard for progress/plan-adherence checks). Environment provides binary task reward only for final success-rate scoring, not as a per-step correction signal
iteration_structure: iterative-refine within a single task episode (in-situ reflections at fixed reflection-frequency intervals, single trial of up to 50 turns per task); constitution is curated cross-task via periodic summarization. Contrasts with Reflexion's episodic-retry-with-reset (up to 15 trials)
reflection_object: Primarily structured rules/constitution (a compact, categorized set of guiding principles) distilled from task and environment experiences; also the action trajectory and prompt/context (the constitution is injected into the agent's system prompt). The constitution holds environment-level (high) and task-level (low) knowledge.
requires_training: none (no fine-tuning; prompt-based guidance only — explicitly contrasts itself with Constitutional AI's fine-tuning approach)
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge (the agent/Meta-advisor LLM generates and curates its own reflections); plus a symbolic verifier (regular expressions) for progress tracking. No trained reward model. Reflection/summarization is triggered by fixed hyperparameters rather than an LLM-as-a-Judge
distillation_target: structured-rules/constitution (a compact 'OmniC' rule book of categorized, summarized reflections persisted as structured long-term memory). Also functions as a prompt artifact when injected into another agent
emergent_vs_engineered: prompt/scaffold-engineered — reflection is induced by hand-crafted reflection prompts, reflection categories (Abstract/Error/Progress), symbolic regex templates, and fixed reflection/summarization-frequency hyperparameters; not RL-emergent
memory_type: playbook/cheatsheet (the 'constitution' / OmniC = categorized, summarized rule book) serving as structured long-term memory; transient progress-tracking notes act as a short-term scratchpad within an episode
memory_persistence: cross-task and cross-session within an environment for Abstract and Error reflections (environment-level long-term memory shared across tasks/sessions); within-episode (short-term) for Progress reflections
memory_curation_mechanism: self-summarized/curated — the reflection LLM performs periodic summarization (every s_freq tasks) that transforms unstructured episodic traces into an organized rule book, reducing redundancy and preventing unbounded growth. Ablation shows over-summarization can degrade performance by omitting useful information
error_localization_granularity: step-level / block-level — in-situ reflections analyze recent trajectory steps and observations at fixed intervals; symbolic regex evaluates the most recent observation. Operates at finer granularity than holistic outcome-level retry (Error reflection targets specific mistakes; Progress reflection monitors sub-task completion order)
intra_task_vs_inter_task: both — intra-task (in-situ Progress and Error reflections refine within a single execution episode) and inter-task (Abstract/Error reflections accumulate into a constitution transferred across tasks, sessions, and even across model backbones in Co-operative mode)
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: mid-trajectory-recovery — in-situ reflections generated at periodic intervals within a single task let the agent recover from mistakes in-flight (reducing iterations needed), unlike Reflexion's avoidance-via-retry-next-episode; constitution also enables avoidance on future tasks
task_domains: embodied/games, decision-making, planning, web/grid navigation, tool-use (household interaction, grid navigation, symbolic planning)
benchmarks: ALFWorld (unseen split), BabyAI (AgentBoard test split), PDDL (Gripper, Blocksworld, Barman, Tyreworld domains; AgentBoard test split)
headline_result: Self-sustaining mode, averaged across models (Qwen3-4B, Gemini-2.0, GPT-4), absolute success-rate gains over the 15-trial Reflexion baseline despite using only a single trial: +10.3% on ALFWorld, +23.8% on BabyAI, +8.3% on PDDL. OmniReflect is best in 7/9 settings. Co-operative mode with GPT-4 Meta-advisor improves ReAct agents by +28% (ALFWorld), +29% (BabyAI), +20.9% (PDDL) from one calibration example per task type with no extra test-time inferences
baselines: ReAct (single trial, 50 turns) and Reflexion (up to 15 trials x 50 turns). Conceptually contrasted with Constitutional AI, Self-Consistency / Universal Self-Consistency, Self-Refine, MemoryBank/RET-LLM/MemGPT, and automatic prompt-optimization methods
gains_vs_baseline: Vs strongest baseline Reflexion (15 trials): Self-sustaining single-trial OmniReflect averages +10.3% (ALFWorld), +23.8% (BabyAI), +8.3% (PDDL). Example single-cell deltas (best OmniReflect variant vs Reflexion): ALFWorld GPT-4 100.0 vs 84.1 (+15.9); BabyAI Qwen3-4B 73.2 vs 44.1 (+29.1); PDDL Qwen3-4B 31.7 vs 11.7 (+20.0). Reflexion still wins 2/9 (Gemini-2.0 on ALFWorld; GPT-4 on PDDL). 24/27 Co-operative Meta-advisor/ReAct pairs beat ReAct-only
compute_cost_profile: Far cheaper than Reflexion: Reflexion needs up to ~764 LLM calls per task; OmniReflect-Neural reduces this to under 80 (~700 fewer inferences) at comparable interaction-turn counts to ReAct. OmniReflect-Symbolic adds zero LLM calls for reflection. Co-operative mode adds zero extra test-time inferences (constitution pre-injected into prompt). Still adds LLM calls vs plain ReAct; unfiltered constitution can inflate context for small-context models
known_limitations: Adds extra LLM calls (deployment overhead); constitutions are integrated without filtering, which can increase cost for limited-context models and introduce noise; evaluated only in embodied agentic settings (ALFWorld/BabyAI/PDDL), not broader reasoning/planning; uses simple ReAct backbone (no Self-Consistency etc.); symbolic regex requires manual design/annotation. Effectiveness depends on Meta-advisor reasoning quality (weak abstraction or cross-scale transfer fails in a few configs)
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: external-tool/verifier (symbolic regular-expression progress checks extend AgentBoard) combined with self-verify; no ground-truth label leakage into the correction loop (final reward used only for scoring success rate, not as a per-step oracle). Self-correction works in a single trial without oracle answers
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive — single-trial in-situ reflection improves success rate over both ReAct and multi-trial Reflexion in most settings (best in 7/9 Self-sustaining and 24/27 Co-operative configurations), though task-dependent (Symbolic best on structured ALFWorld/PDDL, Neural best on dynamic BabyAI; 2-3 configurations regress)
calibration_effect: not-measured (the paper does not report probability calibration / confidence metrics; 'calibration set' refers to a small set of bootstrap tasks for the Meta-advisor, not confidence calibration)
failure_attribution_capability: classifies-failure-mode (via Error reflections that diagnose mistakes from trajectory analysis) and attributes-failing-step (Progress reflections monitor sub-task completion order); not a dedicated failure-attribution benchmark method
failure_mode_addressed: Targets superficial/ineffective self-reflection and siloed per-trial reflection (by accumulating a shared constitution), mismatched world-model assumptions / hallucinated environment knowledge (Abstract reflections), recurring planning inefficiencies and error-loops (Error reflections), and premature or out-of-order sub-task execution / underthinking (Progress reflections). Also addresses memory drift/unbounded-growth of prior memory systems via summarization
builds_on: ReAct (Yao et al. 2022); Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2024); Self-Refine (Madaan et al. 2024); Constitutional AI (Bai et al. 2022); AgentBoard (Ma et al. 2024, for benchmarks and base regular expressions); benchmark environments ALFWorld (Shridhar et al. 2020), BabyAI (Chevalier-Boisvert et al. 2018), PDDL (Silver & Chitnis 2020). Related to MemoryBank, RET-LLM, MemGPT for memory
reasoning_model_native: no — evaluated on non-reasoning-native backbones (Qwen3-4B, Gemini-2.0, GPT-4/GPT-4o); reflection is externally scaffolded via prompts and a constitution rather than relying on a model with built-in chain-of-thought reflection. Not specifically targeted at o1/R1-style reasoning models
on_policy_distillation_link: Indirect: distills the agent's own on-policy task experiences (trajectories) into a reusable constitution that re-guides the same or another agent; in Co-operative mode a stronger Meta-advisor distills constitutions consumed by a weaker on-policy agent (a prompt-level, weight-free analogue of skill/experience distillation, not gradient-based on-policy distillation)
sample_efficiency: High: Self-sustaining mode reaches its reported gains in a single trial (vs Reflexion's up to 15 trials), and reflections are generated only every r_freq=10 turns; Co-operative mode derives an effective constitution from as little as one calibration example per task type
